---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: minor
michi-node: minor

michi-core: a value's rules now hold for its whole life, because the types with a rule across their fields keep those fields private. A `RetryConfig` can no longer get a zero `max_delay` after `try_new`, which turned a server's `Retry-After: 60` into an immediate retry. A `DomainError` can no longer have its code or retry flag changed behind the builder, which left a retryable timeout without its "verify first" hint. A `PartialSuccess` can no longer list one operation as both completed and failed. `CallToolResult.structured_content` is now an `Option<JsonObject>`, checked when it is built in every build, so every result serializes. The wire output is unchanged.

Breaking: `DomainError`'s fields are private. Read them with `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()` and `is_retryable()`, and use `class()` to classify. `render()` and `render_json()` are now `render(OutputFormat::Text)` and `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. `retry_after` takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`, and the new `context(prefix)` replaces writing to `message`. `michi_core::Error` and `michi_core::Result` are removed; nothing in michi produced them. `RetryConfig`'s fields are private; read them with `max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()` and `jitter_factor()`, and build one with `new`, `try_new` or `default`. `PartialSuccess::new` is now `PartialSuccess::try_new`, which returns `DuplicateOpIndex` when an index repeats. Its fields are read with `completed()`, `failed()` and `skipped()`. `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason) and `SkippedOp`. `Pipeline` has no `id`, so `Pipeline::new(steps)` takes only the steps. `CallToolResult::new` takes `Option<JsonObject>`; `CallToolResult::try_new` is removed (use `JsonObject::try_new`). `StatusResponse::with_hints` is renamed `hints`, and `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]`.

Also: `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass` implement `Hash`, `ErrorCode` implements `Display` (its label), and `DomainError` implements `PartialEq`.

michi-pipeline: `StepId` and `RunId` implement `FromStr` and `Borrow<str>`, so `"fetch".parse::<StepId>()` works and a map keyed by id can be looked up with a `&str`. `AttemptRecord` implements `Eq`. `RunRecord::to_pipeline()` no longer carries the run id (read it with `run_id()`). An ambiguous timeout's `DomainError` now carries one verify-first hint, not none: the conversion used to write `retryable = false` past the builder and so dropped core's hint.

michi-node: Breaking: `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]` in place of `OpRef[]`. It throws when an `index` appears twice across the three lists, and when a completed operation has a `reason`. Before, a duplicate rendered as two outcomes and the reason was dropped without a word.

Migration: replace `e.code`, `e.message`, `e.retryable` and the other field reads with the getters. Replace `e.render()` with `e.render(OutputFormat::Text)`, and replace `cfg.max_delay` and the other config fields with `cfg.max_delay()`. Replace `PartialSuccess::new(c, f, s)` with `PartialSuccess::try_new(c, f, s)?`, `OpRef::new` with `CompletedOp::new` or `SkippedOp::new`, and `Pipeline::new(id, steps)` with `Pipeline::new(steps)`. Wrap structured content as `Some(JsonObject::try_new(text)?)`. Replace `michi_core::Error::Domain(e)` with `e`.

michi-core: minor

michi-core: every outcome composes into one `AgentResponse`. `error(DomainError)` adds the error block, which renders first, and `partial_success(name, ps)`, `status(s)`, `pipeline(name, p)` and `already_done(operation, summary)` add sections. Their hints and recovery hints join the response's one `help` and `recovery` block. A batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is now one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result. NAPI: `AgentResponse` gains `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `alreadyDone`, so `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` now cover errors too.

michi-core: Breaking: one error JSON shape. `DomainError::render(OutputFormat::Json)`, its serde form and its `schemars` schema are the response envelope: `{"body", "error": {"code", "message", "causes", "retryable"}, "hints", "recovery", "isError"}`. `recovery` is always an array, as in every response. Before, the JSON was `{isError, error, message, causes, retryable, hints, recovery}`, with `error` the code and `recovery` an object or `null`. Read `error.code` where you read `error`, and `recovery[0]` where you read `recovery`. The text render is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: `PartialSuccess::render` is one table, `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, with a row per operation sorted by index. Before, it wrote a quoted summary line and separate `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` tables. The failed operations' recovery table is unchanged. An empty report renders `partial_success: []` and `totalCount: 0`. JS `renderPartialSuccess` renders the same.

michi-core: Breaking: an empty `Pipeline` renders `step: []` and `totalCount: 0`, and a `StatusResponse` with no items renders `items: []` and `totalCount: 0`. This is the same empty list as any other section. `michi-pipeline`'s `RunRecord::render` of a run with no steps changes with it.

==> .changeset/durable-starts-off-scheduler.md <==
---
michi-pipeline: minor
---

Breaking: `DurableObserver::record_start` now runs on a blocking thread owned by its step, not inline in the scheduler loop. Parallel steps save their start markers concurrently (8 steps with a 100 ms save: 830 ms before, 114 ms after), so `record_start` must be safe to call concurrently and in any order across steps. A step still runs only after its own `record_start` returns `Ok`, and looks at the run again after the save: a cancel or fail-fast stop during it ends the step `Skipped(Cancelled)`. A deadline group's window now opens before the first step's save, so the save counts against it; a step whose window ends during its save ends `Failed` with `DeadlinePassed` without being invoked.

---
michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor

michi-core: what a response reports about itself now has one source each, so its text and JSON cannot contradict each other. A section's `truncated` is derived (its total is above its count), the budget's `sections[n]` roll-up is written from the response's own sections, and the budget's `truncated` is also true whenever a section was cut. The root keys michi writes itself are one reserved list for every writer, and it now includes the error document's keys, so a successful response can no longer render an `error:` / `message:` document from caller data. A provenance label `fingerprint` is always rejected, because it read exactly like the real fingerprint.

Breaking: `Section`'s fields are private; read them with `name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()` and `truncated()`. `Section::truncated(bool)` and `Section::returned_count(n)` are removed; a text section that stands for several items is `Section::text_with_count(name, body, n)`, and `SectionBody::Text` is now `Text { text, count }`. `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section()` are removed, and the budget's JSON no longer has a `sections` array (the response's `sections` carries those counts). `truncated_section` now takes `(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)` and builds the rows from `outcome.kept`. `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code` join `totalCount`, `help` and `recovery` as reserved: as a type name (`render_toon`, `list`), a KV key (`render_kv`, `kv_items`) or a section name they are a validation error, and the error messages list the reserved keys.

Migration: `.truncated_section(Section::toon(name, f, rows), &outcome, g)` becomes `.truncated_section(name, f, &outcome, |item| row_of(item), g)`. Drop `.truncated(..)` on sections and `.section(SectionCost::new(..))` on budgets. Rename any KV key or list named after a reserved key (for example a `message` field becomes `commit_message`). In JavaScript, `renderKv`, `renderToon` and `kvItems` reject the same reserved names.

==> .changeset/legacy-removal-render-perf.md <==
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: `ToonOptions` is the list alone. `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` (and their builders) are removed; `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse`, which places each once for the whole response. `render_toon` writes the list entry and the `truncated` block. `render_kv(items)` lost its `total_count` and `hints` parameters. NAPI: `renderToon` no longer takes `totalCount`, `hints` or `truncationHint`, and `renderKv(items)` no longer takes `totalCount` or `hints`; `AgentResponse.items`, `kvItems` and `truncationHint` keep them.

Migration: `render_toon(&ToonOptions::new(..).total_count(Some(n)).hints(h))` becomes `AgentResponse::new(name).section(Section::toon(name, fields, rows).total_count(Some(n))).hint(..)` rendered with `render(OutputFormat::Text)`. For hints on a standalone list, `append_hints(&mut out, &hints)`.

michi-core: Breaking: one definitive empty state. `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed. An empty `Toon` section, and so an untouched `AgentResponse`, now renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (it rendered `name: []` alone). Use `AgentResponse::new(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`) where you called `empty_state`. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing.

michi-core: `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` no longer copy every row on each call. They validate and render a borrowed view of the section's rows: 1,000 rows took 2,015 allocations to render and 2,011 for `is_error()`, and now take about what `render_toon` takes. `toon::list` no longer keeps every parsed item until the rows are built. Output is unchanged.

==> .changeset/napi-structure-output-bound.md <==
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: the NAPI byte budget is now 16 MiB, was 64 MiB, per call and per `AgentResponse`. It limited input only, and a render writes up to 19 times the bytes it holds (a control character is 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON, 19 in `toCallToolResult()`). At 64 MiB a maximal response took 3.2 GiB and 25 s in `toCallToolResult()`, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. At 16 MiB every render is under that limit, so a response renders or is rejected before anything is rendered. In JavaScript, a call with more than 16 MiB of strings, or an `AgentResponse` that would hold more, now throws `input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` or `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` where up to 64 MiB was accepted. A name is charged for every place a render writes it: a `truncated` row repeats the cell's field name (and the section name when two or more sections are cut) for every cut cell, and the `totalCount` table repeats the section name. A 4 KiB field name with 1,000 rows of one 201-char cell holds 261 KB and would render to about 100 times that. `AgentResponse.items`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `renderToon` charge a field name (and a section name) once for each string cell over 200 chars, `partialSuccess` and `pipeline` charge their section name twice (its header and its `totalCount` row), and `hint` and `recoveryHint` charge 1 and 4 bytes more than their text. Normal responses (short names, cells under 200 chars) are charged almost the same as before. A render is at most 19 times the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface, and tests measure it over a matrix of hostile responses. Every other limit, error message and TypeScript type is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: `michi_core::napi` (behind the `napi` feature) now exposes only `num`. The typed functions `render_toon(JsToonOptions)`, `render_hints`, `append_hints`, `render_recovery`, `render_kv`, `render_status`, `render_domain_error`, `render_already_done`, `render_partial_success`, `render_pipeline`, `already_done` and the `JsAgentResponse` Rust methods are private; the JS exports are the only entry points. `napi.rs` is split by concern into `napi/*.rs`.

michi-core: `ErrorCode` gains `ALL` and `FromStr`, and `StepStatus` gains `ALL` and `from_labels` (with `StepLabelError`): the inverse of `label()` and `reason()`, built from the same tables.

==> .changeset/pipeline-error-redaction.md <==
---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: minor
---

Breaking: converting an `ExecutionError` to a `DomainError` no longer puts step text in the trusted `message`. The message is now fixed text (`http 502`, `the step reported an error`, `step panicked`, `deadline passed`), and what the step or server said (an HTTP body, a `failed()` message, a panic payload) is one entry in `causes`, redacted and cut to 512 bytes including the `…` marker. Read it from `causes`, not `message`.

`DomainError::from_error` and `from_error_with_causes` now use the new `michi_core::redact::redact_common_shapes`. On top of URL userinfo it redacts the value of `token=`, `access_token=`, `api_key=`, `password=` and similar pairs (quoted, `'x'`, JSON `"password": "x"` or JSON-escaped `\"x\"`, and after the fullwidth `＝` and `：`), `Key: value` headers (`X-Api-Key:`, `Cookie:`, `Set-Cookie:`), the credential after a scheme word (`Authorization: Basic ...`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Digest`), and `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `npm_` and `pypi-` tokens. Text with `token: ...` or similar in prose is redacted too, which is the safe direction. The scan is linear in the text, also for a long line of `key="` pairs and for a long text of URLs (`redact_url_userinfo` no longer rescans the rest of the text once per URL, which made a 1 MiB body of URLs take minutes). `redact_url_userinfo` also handles JSON-escaped (`https:\/\/`) and percent-encoded (`https%3A%2F%2F`) URLs and a `"` inside a password. This is best effort: the docs list what is and is not covered.

`redact_secrets` copies an existing `[REDACTED]` through where no known secret matches, so a secret such as `RED` no longer turns the marker into `[[REDACTED]ACTED]` on a second pass; redacting twice is a no-op unless a secret contains `[`. A known secret that starts with or contains the marker (`[REDACTED]private-tail`) still wins over the copy-through and is removed whole.

==> .changeset/response-consistency.md <==
---
michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: a response with an error and an invalid section (or two blocks writing one root key) reports both, and the same on every surface (text, JSON, `render_for`, `to_call_tool_result`, NAPI): the caller's error leads and stays the JSON `error`, and each validation failure is added after its causes as `toon_validation_failed: <message>` (or `kv_validation_failed`). `isError` stays true. Several failures (two failed sections, or a failed section beside a collision) are one `error` object too: the caller's error, or without one the first failure, with every other failure as a cause, never a collision on `error`.

michi-core: Breaking: a validation failure is an `error` object in JSON, `{"code": "toon_validation_failed", "message": …, "causes": [], "retryable": false}` (or `kv_validation_failed`), the same keys as every other error. Before, it was `isError: true` with no `error` object. The text is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: a section's JSON `totalCount` follows the text's rule. It appears when the total exceeds the rows and is `0` for an empty list, and is left out for a total at or below the rows (it was the declared value whenever one was set). The budget roll-up's `total` column follows the same rule, so it shows `null` where it showed a total equal to the rows, and `0` for an empty list. `Section::total()` still returns the value as given.

michi-core: Breaking: `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` replaces only the hints added with `hint()` and `hints()`. A `status()` report's hints and a `truncated_section()`'s `showing N of M` line are kept; before, `hints()` dropped them.

==> .changeset/napi-structure-output-bound.md <==
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: the NAPI byte budget is now 16 MiB, was 64 MiB, per call and per `AgentResponse`. It limited input only, and a render writes up to 19 times the bytes it holds (a control character is 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON, 19 in `toCallToolResult()`). At 64 MiB a maximal response took 3.2 GiB and 25 s in `toCallToolResult()`, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. At 16 MiB every render is under that limit, so a response renders or is rejected before anything is rendered. In JavaScript, a call with more than 16 MiB of strings, or an `AgentResponse` that would hold more, now throws `input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` or `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` where up to 64 MiB was accepted. A name is charged for every place a render writes it: a `truncated` row repeats the cell's field name (and the section name when two or more sections are cut) for every cut cell, and the `totalCount` table repeats the section name. A 4 KiB field name with 1,000 rows of one 201-char cell holds 261 KB and would render to about 100 times that. `AgentResponse.items`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `renderToon` charge a field name (and a section name) once for each string cell over 200 chars, `partialSuccess` and `pipeline` charge their section name twice (its header and its `totalCount` row), and `hint` and `recoveryHint` charge 1 and 4 bytes more than their text. Normal responses (short names, cells under 200 chars) are charged almost the same as before. A render is at most 19 times the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface, and tests measure it over a matrix of hostile responses. Every other limit, error message and TypeScript type is unchanged.

Breaking: converting an `ExecutionError` to a `DomainError` no longer puts step text in the trusted `message`. The message is now fixed text (`http 502`, `the step reported an error`, `step panicked`, `deadline passed`), and what the step or server said (an HTTP body, a `failed()` message, a panic payload) is one entry in `causes`, redacted and cut to 512 bytes including the `…` marker. Read it from `causes`, not `message`.

`DomainError::from_error` and `from_error_with_causes` now use the new `michi_core::redact::redact_common_shapes`. On top of URL userinfo it redacts the value of `token=`, `access_token=`, `api_key=`, `password=` and similar pairs (quoted, `'x'`, JSON `"password": "x"` or JSON-escaped `\"x\"`, and after the fullwidth `＝` and `：`), `Key: value` headers (`X-Api-Key:`, `Cookie:`, `Set-Cookie:`), the credential after a scheme word (`Authorization: Basic ...`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Digest`), and `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `npm_` and `pypi-` tokens. Text with `token: ...` or similar in prose is redacted too, which is the safe direction. The scan is linear in the text, also for a long line of `key="` pairs and for a long text of URLs (`redact_url_userinfo` no longer rescans the rest of the text once per URL, which made a 1 MiB body of URLs take minutes). `redact_url_userinfo` also handles JSON-escaped (`https:\/\/`) and percent-encoded (`https%3A%2F%2F`) URLs and a `"` inside a password. This is best effort: the docs list what is and is not covered.

`redact_secrets` copies an existing `[REDACTED]` through where no known secret matches, so a secret such as `RED` no longer turns the marker into `[[REDACTED]ACTED]` on a second pass; redacting twice is a no-op unless a secret contains `[`. A known secret that starts with or contains the marker (`[REDACTED]private-tail`) still wins over the copy-through and is removed whole.

docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md:202:- **Output size:** the byte budget bounds what a render writes, not only what it reads. On every surface, a render is at most **19 times the bytes held, plus 4 KiB**. A control character is the worst case for a string: six bytes in the text (`\u0001`), seven in the JSON `body` (the text, escaped again) and six in the raw `sections`, `error` and `hints` copies, so one held byte is at most 6 + 7 + 6 = 19 bytes across the text and the JSON that `toCallToolResult()` returns together. A name is written in more places than that, so the budget charges each name for every place a writer can put it, not once: a `truncated` row writes the cell's field name, and, when two or more sections are cut, its section name, again for every cut cell (a string cell longer than 200 chars; no export changes that cap), so a field name is charged once per cut-capable cell of its column, and the type name or an outcome section's name once per cut-capable cell of its table; a section's name is charged twice (its `name[N]{…}:` header or `name: []` line and its row of the `totalCount` table; the type name's second charge is the one made when the response is built); a hint is charged one byte more than its length and a recovery hint four, for the row and the JSON object that hold them. Before, each name was charged once, and a 4 KiB field name with 1,000 rows of one 201-char cell (261 KB held) rendered to 24.8 MB of text and 29.1 MB of JSON, 95 and 112 times what it held; at 60,000 rows, under the old cap, `renderText()` failed with `Failed to convert rust String into napi string`. That table now holds about 4.4 KB per row, so 3,859 rows fit and 60,000 are rejected with `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` (`input byte total N …` for `renderToon`, which charges the same names for its one list). The one-shot renders write text only: at most 6 bytes per byte charged, 26 per cell, 4 per row and 400 per other entry, which the counts cap under 200 MiB (a compile-time assertion). The tests render a matrix of hostile responses (every escape trigger and multi-byte characters; 4 KiB type, section and field names; cut cells in every composed section; numbers at their widest; each tiny item at its cap, alone) and assert that no surface passes the bound, with mutants (a factor of 18, a field or section name left uncharged) failing it; the Node suite builds the largest hostile table the budget accepts and measures all three formats against V8's string limit (about 512 MiB, `2^29 - 24` characters). At the old 64 MiB cap a maximal response (60 one-MiB control-character values) wrote 377 MB of text on a 1.2 GiB heap, and `toCallToolResult()` took 25 s and 3.2 GiB; at 16 MiB the worst case is 304 MiB, under the string limit, so a response either renders in every format or is rejected by the budget before anything is rendered. The largest accepted plain one (15 one-MiB control-character values) took 0.6 s and 348 MiB for `renderText()`, 2.8 s and 648 MiB for `renderJson()`, and 5.5 s and 838 MiB for `toCallToolResult()`, in a debug build.

docs/spec/03-rust-api.md:668:- `redact_url_userinfo` replaces the `user:password@` part of every `scheme://…` URL. A URL ends at whitespace, a quote, a backtick, `<` or `>`; everything up to the last `@` inside it is userinfo, so a password containing `@` or `/` is removed whole. A URL with no userinfo but an `@` later in its path (`https://host/pkg@1.2`) is over-redacted; that is the safe direction. Email addresses are not URLs and pass through. Also matched: the JSON-escaped separator `:\/\/`, the percent-encoded separator `%3A%2F%2F` (userinfo ends at the last `@` or `%40`), and a `"` or `'` inside the password (the text after the quote is searched for an `@` until a `/`, `\`, `?` or `#`; `"https://host","k":"a@b"` is over-redacted).
docs/spec/03-rust-api.md:669:- `redact_common_shapes` is `redact_url_userinfo` plus the value of any `key=value` pair or `Key: value` header whose key names a secret, plus well-known token shapes. Keys: `key`, `sig`, `auth`, `pwd`, anything ending `_key`, `_sig` or `_auth`, starting `auth_`, or containing `token`, `secret`, `passw`, `signature`, `apikey`, `api_key`, `credential`, `authoriz` or `cookie` (case-insensitive, `-` read as `_`). The separator may be `=`, `:`, or their fullwidth forms, with blanks around it, and the key may be quoted or JSON-escaped, so `{"password": "x"}`, `'token': 'x'`, `\"token\":\"x\"`, `X-Api-Key: x` and `a=1&token=x` are all covered. A quoted value runs to its closing quote (`\` escapes honored, a newline ends an unclosed one) and keeps its quotes. After a scheme word (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Negotiate`, `NTLM`, `Bot`, `Digest`) the credential is redacted and the word kept: `Authorization: Basic [REDACTED]`. `Digest` and cookie keys (`Cookie:`, `Set-Cookie:`) take the rest of the line. Any other value runs to whitespace, `&`, a quote, a backtick, `)`, `<` or `>`. `key://` is a URL, not a pair. The work is linear in the text, URLs included (`tests/scaling.rs`): `redact_url_userinfo` is one forward pass that looks for the next separator form, a URL's end and its last `@` without rescanning text it already examined, and `tests/redact_differential.rs` pins its output to the simple per-URL version it replaced. Token shapes: `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`, `npm_` and `pypi-` followed by 16 or more token characters, and `Bearer ` followed by 16 or more. It repeats until the text stops changing, so redacting twice equals redacting once. A fuzz target (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/redact.rs`) checks that and that a planted secret does not survive in any covered shape.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:36:- `AgentResponse`/`JsAgentResponse` is exported, along with `renderHints()`/`appendHints()`/`renderRecovery()`/`renderToon()`/`emptyState()`/`truncate()`.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:45:- **A related bug surfaced during this reconciliation and got fixed alongside it:** independent of which Rust-side type `params` used, `AgentResponse::render_json()`'s JSON _output_ was, for a time, stringifying every param value regardless of its `KvValue` variant (`{"seconds":"30"}` instead of `{"seconds":30}`) — which would have defeated the point of a typed enum entirely.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:46:- `render_json()` now serializes `Int`/`Float`/`Bool` as native JSON literals, `Text` as a JSON string, `Missing` as `null`, so both the Rust-side and JSON-output representations carry real type information.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:80:- **That's not how it shipped.** `crates/michi-pipeline` defines its own `ExecutionError` enum (`Http`, `Timeout`, `Failed`, `CircuitOpen`, `StepFailed`, `Cancelled`, `Interrupted`, `AmbiguousOutcome`, `Panicked`, and since 0.6 `DeadlinePassed`; plan validation has its own `PlanError` since the 2026-10-21 redesign) rather than adding variants to `michi_core::Error`. `impl From<ExecutionError> for DomainError` converts at the boundary instead. `michi_core::Error` itself still has only `InvalidInput`/`NotFound`/`Domain` — verified against current source, not extended. This keeps `michi-pipeline`'s error surface independently versioned alongside the crate it belongs to, consistent with the "independent release cadence" rationale above, rather than coupling it back into `michi-core`.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:114:- **Sections extend `AgentResponse` rather than arriving as a parallel `BatchResponse` type.** A second response type would duplicate hints, recovery, audience routing, `human_content`, and the whole `to_call_tool_result()` path, and would leave every consumer choosing between two builders on a distinction (one section or several) they often learn only at render time. `items()`/`kv_items()` stay as one-section sugar over the same storage, and a zero- or one-section response renders byte-for-byte as it does today — the existing `insta` snapshots are the test, so multi-section support is a minor bump, not a major one. Widening `PartialSuccess`'s `completed`/`skipped` from `Vec<String>` to index-bearing `OpRef` **is** a major bump, since `completed[2]:` becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:` and rendered output differs. Taken now because there is no published consumer to break; taken at all because `Vec<String>` cannot express `results[i]` ↔ `ops[i]`, and that correspondence is the whole point of a batch response.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:116:- **Never fail closed on overflow — written down here so no future primitive regresses to it.** Serena's `find_symbol` returns _no content_ once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded; the agent is left to guess a narrower query knowing nothing about what it missed. Every michi overflow path does the opposite: partial results, `returned_count`/`total_count`, and a hint naming the refinement. This is also why the envelope carries no pagination cursor — MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one, so a cursor here would be a private convention no client honors.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:436:- **Empty list (§9.1, §6):** `issues[0]{}:` → `issues: []`. An empty field list is a syntax error and the legacy `key[0]:` header must not be emitted. `empty_state()` and `Pipeline::render()` follow.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:444:- **Root document and whitespace (§5, §12):** a list document is a root object (list entry, `totalCount`, `help`), the empty type name is the quoted empty key `""`, and documents end without a trailing newline: `render_toon`, `list`, `ToonDocument::render`, `empty_state(_with_hints)`, `Pipeline::render`, and every `AgentResponse` text output (TOON and KV paths, so the two end the same way; the JSON `body` likewise). Block helpers meant for concatenation — `render_hints`, `append_hints`, `render_kv`, `render_recovery`, `DomainError::render`, `StatusResponse::render`, `PartialSuccess::render` — keep their trailing newline, and `append_hints` starts its block on a new line when the buffer does not end in one.

docs/spec/06-decisions.md:818:The architecture and security audits of 0.10.0 rendered documents that contradicted themselves: a section with `totalCount: 5` and `"truncated": false`, a budget roll-up naming a `ghost` section beside two real ones, a success response whose KV items read exactly like a `DomainError` (`error:`, `message:`, `exit_code:`), and a provenance label posing as the fingerprint. docs/spec/06-decisions.md:822:- **The budget roll-up is derived.** `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section` are removed. `sections[n]{name,returned,total,truncated}:` is written from the response's own sections at render time, still only with two or more. `BudgetSummary` keeps only what michi cannot know: ceilings, usage and `truncated`, now meaning "the budget dropped something the sections cannot show". The rendered `truncated` is that flag or any cut section, so `budget: truncated: false` cannot sit above a cut section. Wire change: the budget's JSON loses its `sections` array; the response's `sections` already carries the same counts.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:823:- **One reserved-root-key list.** `toon::RESERVED_ROOT_KEYS` (crate-internal) is `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`, `truncated`, `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`. `ToonDocument::validate` (so `render_toon`, `list()` and `empty_state`), `render_kv` and the response's collision check all read it, and the `InvalidTypeName` / `ReservedKey` messages print it. Before, the three writers checked three lists (3, 4 and 7 keys), and `error`/`message` were claimed only by a failed section. The error document's keys are reserved even on success, so caller data cannot render an error document while `isError` is false. `causes` is in the list too: it is the fourth key of `DomainError::render`. Breaking: a KV key, type name or section name from that list (a commit's `message`, say) is now a validation error; rename it.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:833:- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst render is 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering. A `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit, and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (exact, but it adds a second accounting table that must follow every escape rule, and plain ASCII gains nothing), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate).
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:834:- **Compatibility:** inputs over 16 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Pre-1.0, and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:841:- **One definitive empty state.** `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are deleted. They rendered `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`, while an untouched `AgentResponse` and an empty `Toon` section rendered `name: []` alone, so an agent saw two shapes from one library. The decision is the definitive one: an empty `Toon` section (and so an untouched response) renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`, so a reader sees "zero results" and not a list that might have been dropped. A larger `totalCount` the caller set stays as set. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing: it has no list to be empty. The JSON `sections` entry keeps the caller's facts (`returnedCount: 0`; `totalCount` only when set), so `truncated` stays derived from set total and count. (Superseded by "Response consistency": the JSON entry reports `totalCount: 0` like the text; `truncated` is still derived from the set total.) **Output moves (the only ones in this change):** `AgentResponse::new(n)` with nothing added, and a response holding an empty `Toon` section, gain a `totalCount: 0` line; two or more sections that report a total (an empty list now does) merge into the `totalCount[N]{section,total}:` table. A reserved type name still renders the `toon_validation_failed` error block, as `empty_state` did.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:858:- **States the domain forbids:** `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason, so none can be dropped) and `SkippedOp`; the JS `renderPartialSuccess` takes the same two shapes, rejects a non-null `reason` on a completed op and throws on a repeated index. `Pipeline.id` is removed: nothing rendered it, `renderPipeline` passed an empty string, and `RunRecord::to_pipeline` filled it for no reader. Rejected: rendering it (`pipeline: <id>`), which would change a document no consumer asked to change; `RunRecord::run_id()` already gives the id.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:860:- **`michi_core::Error` and `Result` are removed.** No michi API returned them (every fallible function has its own error type; `michi-pipeline` converts to `DomainError`), monokl builds `DomainError` directly, and `Error::InvalidInput`/`NotFound` duplicated `ErrorCode` minus hints, recovery and causes. ADR 9 says such surface goes before 1.0. `class()` and `is_retryable()` live on `DomainError`; `is_retryable()` is `true` exactly when `class()` is `Transient`.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:861:- **One convention for builders and getters** (spec 03, "API conventions"): builders are bare and consuming (`x(v)` sets or appends one, `xs(vec)` replaces a list); getters are bare, `is_x()` for a `bool`, and `get_x()` only when a builder of the same type holds the bare name, as `std::process::Command::get_args` does. Considered: `with_x` builders (would rename every builder in core and `michi-pipeline` to free a few getter names) and getters named after their type (`recovery_hint()` would read as `AgentResponse`'s appending builder of the same name). Applied: `StatusResponse::with_hints` became `hints`; `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]` like every other renderer; `DomainError::render()` and `render_json()` became `render(OutputFormat)`, like `AgentResponse`; text-only types keep `render()`. `DomainError::context(prefix)` replaces the field write `e.message = format!(…)` the docs used to suggest, and `retry_after(None)` clears a delay.

# michi-node

## 0.10.0

_2026-11-15 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/compare/michi-node@0.9.0...michi-node@0.10.0)_

- Released together with the `michi` fixed group.

## 0.9.0

- Released together with the `michi` fixed group.

## 0.8.0

- michi-core: truncation is reported out of band, and `DomainError::from_error` no longer copies the cause chain.
  
  **Truncated TOON cells.** A cell longer than `max_cell_len` used to end in text such as `(233 more chars — use full=true)`, and a cell whose own data ended the same way was indistinguishable from a real cut. A cut cell now keeps `max_cell_len - 1` chars and ends in a plain `…`, and every cut is listed in a new `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block after the list (`row` is 0-based, `removed` is the chars cut). `truncation_hint` (`truncationHint` in Node) still carries your "get it in full" instruction, now as one extra line in `help[]` (`Cut cells are listed in the truncated block; use full=true for the full value`) that appears only when a cell was cut. `AgentResponse` merges that line into its own hints, in the text, JSON and MCP outputs. `truncated` is now a reserved list type name, like `totalCount`, `help` and `recovery`. `truncate()`, `truncate_inline()` and the Node `truncate()` are unchanged: they still append the in-band suffix, so use them for a single free-text string, not for TOON cells.
  
  Migrate: anything that parsed `(N more chars` out of a cell should read the `truncated` block instead; snapshots of truncated output need regenerating; rename a list type called `truncated`.
  
  **`DomainError::from_error`** now keeps only the error's own `Display` as `message`. The `source()` chain, which often holds URLs with tokens or file paths, stays out of agent-visible output. To keep the chain as `causes`, call the new `DomainError::from_error_with_causes` (the old behaviour). The top-level message is still shown, so make sure it is safe too.
  
  **Docs.** `docs/spec/02-toon-format.md` has a new trust model section: michi guarantees one value cannot create extra lines, fields or cells, and does not stop prompt injection in data; hints, recovery text, error messages, type and field names come from the tool author, never from data.
- Docs: the README now scopes its TOON claims to what was measured (token savings on flat, uniform 100-row lists; retrieval accuracy within noise on single-hop questions), says TOON here is for models reading tool output, and states that `michi-pipeline` resume is at-least-once per step unless the step passes its idempotency key to a downstream that deduplicates. Adds a plain License section.
- `truncate()` reports the cut outside the text. The old form appended `" (N more chars — use hint)"` inside the returned string, which data could imitate, the same flaw cut TOON cells had. Now `truncate(content, max_chars)` returns `Truncated { content, original_chars, removed }`: text that fits comes back unchanged, and a longer text keeps its first `max_chars - 1` chars and ends in a plain `…`. `Truncated::hint(guidance)` gives the `cut N of M chars; …` line for the response's `help[]`.
  
  Migrate: drop the `hint` argument; read `removed` (or call `hint(guidance)`) instead of parsing the suffix; replace `truncate_inline(c, n, h)` with `truncate(c, n).content` and report the cut yourself. In Node, `truncate(content, maxChars)` now returns `{ content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` instead of a string.
- The Node package's TypeScript types lose their `Js` prefix: `ToonValue`, `ToonOptions`, `KvItem`, `RecoveryHint`, `StatusItem`, `FailedOp`, `PipelineStep`, `AlreadyDone`, `ContentBlock`, `Annotations`, `CallToolResult` and `Truncated` (the `AgentResponse` class already had none). Runtime behavior is unchanged except that error messages name the new type (`ToonValue must be an object`). `renderDomainError`'s `code` is now typed as the union of the nine error labels (`'invalid_input' | 'not_found' | ...`) instead of `string`; the runtime still rejects anything else. Migrate: rename the imported types.

content.content:
- **Lifecycle events.** `on_step_started` and `DurableObserver::record_start` fire when a step is dispatched, not when it starts waiting. A step still waiting when the run is cancelled (or fail-fast stops it) ends `Skipped(Cancelled)` without being invoked, and resume runs it again under the limits of the resumed run's options.
`ExecOptions::observer(Arc<dyn StepObserver>)` is called synchronously from the scheduler loop. `on_step_started` fires before a step is spawned and `on_step_finished` fires with each step's terminal `StepRecord`, including skipped steps and, on resume, steps carried over. A closure `Fn(&RunId, &StepRecord)` implements it (finish events only). Persisting each finished record, plus `StepRecord::in_flight(id, name)` for each started one, lets a caller rebuild the run with `RunRecord::from_parts` after a crash. An append-only log is enough: `from_parts` keeps the last record saved for each step, so a step that started and finished rebuilds as finished. Resume then treats a step still `Running` as ambiguous instead of re-running it blindly.
